A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework. Their text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: Sections 6–7 report original sampling and aggregation experiments, diversity analyses, visualizations and LatentRM ablations on three arithmetic benchmarks.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds GPQA/AIME evaluations, explicit-versus-latent reasoning comparisons and variable-length results in Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: MC-dropout, AGN, the LatentRM architecture and contrastive training remain unchanged. Appendix H documents existing sampling procedures. The variable-length experiment changes evaluation settings; length-normalized scoring was already specified in v1 Appendix C.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds GPQA and AIME evaluations across the three retained backbones, extending coverage from arithmetic word problems to Ph.D.-level questions and advanced mathematics. GSM8K-Test, GSM8K-Hard and MultiArith remain.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds deterministic comparators to the existing sampling comparisons. Table 2 introduces evaluated No-CoT and explicit CoT baselines, with deterministic and Coverage@4 results, substantially broadening comparison beyond latent reasoning and aggregation variants.

E3.justification: Appendix F.1 adds an N=4 comparison using decoding steps relative to No-CoT as the computation measure. Appendix F.2 samples COCONUT trajectory lengths uniformly from 4–6 instead of fixing six steps. The original experimental settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds targeted analyses of accuracy versus decoding cost and LatentRM performance with variable-length trajectories. The original component ablations, diversity sweeps, step-wise analyses and t-SNE cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figures 2 and 6 continue reporting means over three runs. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are specified for the added experiments.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds GPQA/AIME coverage results, while Tables 2–3 add accuracy, computation and variable-length outcomes. For example, Table 3 reports 32.44% for the variable-length deterministic baseline and 34.04% for Best-of-16. Original Table 1 values and stochastic/aggregation curves are retained; Figure 2 adds deterministic results.

T1.justification: The latent-reasoning formulation, diversity definition, uncertainty derivations and cumulative-logit ranking argument are retained. V1 Appendices A–B become v2 Appendices B–C. The added conceptual discussion and pseudocode introduce no new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and main conclusion retain the same central claims: stochastic latent sampling enables parallel TTS, and contrastively trained LatentRM enables effective aggregation. Added experiments support these retained contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 removes the deployment and hyperparameter-sensitivity limitations, adds explanations for low GPQA/AIME performance, and introduces interpretations about efficiency and variable-length applicability. Appendix F.1's claim of outperforming explicit CoT overstates Table 2, where selected COCONUT Best-of-4 answers score below deterministic CoT.

D1.justification: V2 adds sampling pseudocode, dataset access links and more precise dataset/model details. The repository link changes from YRYangang/LatentTTS to ModalityDance/LatentTTS; training configuration is retained. Section 5.3 newly prints an invalid dropout default, p=2, which cannot establish an actual experimental change.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds positioning against soft-thinking approaches, citing two additional works. The conclusion adds three ensemble references and a corresponding future direction. The Attention Is All You Need citation is removed; the broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Several introduction, related-work, method and analysis passages are tightened. V2 adds Section 7.3 signposting, reorganizes the appendices and removes the standalone Limitation and Ethics Statement sections. Most main-text prose and section order remain; references adopt numbered entries with expanded annotations.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redesigns the document with branded headers, a shaded full-width abstract and different page geometry. Figure 1 moves to the first page, other displays relocate, Figure 2 gains deterministic lines, and Figure 7, Tables 2–3 and two algorithm boxes are added.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful controls, broader evaluations, variable-length evidence and procedural detail. However, its new efficiency interpretation is misleading: Table 2 reports selected COCONUT Best-of-4 accuracy of 34.5/7.5%, below explicit CoT's 42.9/9.8%; the favorable 46.7% GSM-Test figure is oracle coverage. The invalid new p=2 disclosure and removal of deployment/tuning limitations introduce further reporting weaknesses. These benefits and harms leave the net quality change uncertain.
